paper_title: Optimal Polynomial-Time Compression for Boolean Max CSP
classifications: Theory of computation → Fixed parameter tractability
statement: On the exponential-time front, we have shown that Max d-CNF-SAT is as hard as any Max CSP of degree d as long as negative weights are allowed. Although we were able to get rid of the latter assumption in several cases, there is still a gap in this classification: does improving the running time for any degree-d Max CSP(Γ, N) imply an improvement for Max d-CNF-SAT?
context: We have provided a complete characterization of the optimal compression for Max CSP(Γ) in the case of a Boolean domain. A natural question arises about larger domains. Our approach does not transfer even to the case with a domain of size 3, since there is no unique way to represent functions {0, 1, 2}k → {0, 1} as polynomials. One may consider, e.g., embedding to a Boolean domain or using non-multilinear polynomials, but it is not clear which approach leads to the optimal degree and how to find accompanying lower bounds. On the exponential-time front, we have shown that Max d-CNF-SAT is as hard as any Max CSP of degree d as long as negative weights are allowed. Although we were able to get rid of the latter assumption in several cases, there is still a gap in this classification: does improving the running time for any degree-d Max CSP(Γ, N) imply an improvement for Max d-CNF-SAT?
